match.reason: The bank point covers only physical and chemical weathering, while the new point also requires biological weathering by living things such as roots, which is a missing idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Weathering
card: Weathering is the breaking down of rock where it sits. The rock is not moved away. It is only broken or changed in place.

rock is broken into pieces without changing what it is made of. In frost weathering, water seeps into cracks, freezes and expands, and splits the rock. Heating by day and cooling at night can also crack rock.
rock is changed or dissolved by chemical reactions. Slightly acidic rainwater can slowly dissolve limestone and wear out caves and hollows.
living things break rock down. Plant roots grow into cracks and push them wider. Burrowing animals can also loosen rock.
draft.remember: Weathering breaks rock down in place, by physical, chemical or biological processes.

a.q: Which description best shows weathering rather than another process?
opts: A cliff face cracks and crumbles where it stands
Sand is blown from one dune to a new place
A river carries pebbles downstream to the sea
Waves drop sand to form a beach along a bay
a.why: Weathering breaks rock down where it sits, so the broken rock stays in place. The other options all involve material being moved from one place to another, which is not weathering.
a.clue: Which option has the rock staying where it is?

b.q: A tree grows beside a granite boulder in the Grampians. Over many years its roots grow into a crack and the boulder splits. What type of weathering is this?
opts: Biological weathering, caused by a living thing
Chemical weathering, caused by acidic rain
Physical weathering, caused by freezing water
Biological weathering, caused by burrowing animals
b.why: The roots of a living plant pushed the crack wider, so this is biological weathering. Frost is also a way rock can split, but no water freezing is described here, and no animals are involved.
b.clue: What is making the crack wider?

a.best: A cliff face cracks and crumbles where it stands

b.best: Biological weathering, caused by a living thing
